case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights, rejecting a vagueness challenge to section 211.447.5(6)(a) because the statutory limitation that incarceration alone is not a ground applies only to the subsections it names and not to an unfitness finding under 211.447.5(6)(a).
key_cases.relevance: The opinion measures the father's failure to rectify against the conditions that brought the child into care, which is the legal test for whether court-ordered services succeeded.
key_cases.quote: By the statute's plain terms, subdivision (6) of § 211.447.7 applies only to termination that is pursuant to certain subsections or subdivisions.

key_cases.case_name: Juvenile Officer v. R.O. (In re Z.N.O.)
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the neglect adjudication and change of custody, holding that the circuit court properly confined itself to the allegations pleaded in the petition, that clear and convincing evidence showed the father failed to protect the child from a known abuser, and that a challenge to the specificity of the reasonable-efforts finding was unpreserved absent a Rule 78.07(c) motion.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion addresses the reasonable-efforts finding that must accompany a change of custody and how a parent must preserve a challenge to it.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the circuit court did not misapply Section 211.031 by considering evidence solely related to allegations within the petition.

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of T.W.C. v. Children's Division of the Division of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights, holding that although incarceration alone is not a ground for termination under section 211.447.7(6), it does not excuse a parent from maintaining a continuing relationship through communication and visitation, and that additional services would not have permitted return within an ascertainable period.
key_cases.relevance: T.W.C. addresses whether further court-ordered services such as counseling would have enabled return within an ascertainable period, the statutory reasonable-efforts question.
key_cases.quote: While incarceration alone shall not be grounds for termination of parental rights, section 211.447.7(6), it does not discharge a parent's obligation to provide the child with a continuing relationship

key_cases.holding: The court held that the right to appointed counsel under section 211.462.2 must be strictly applied but is not absolute, arising only when an indigent parent requests counsel, found no abuse of discretion in the handling of counsel and the continuance, and affirmed in part while reversing and remanding in part on other grounds.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion recounts the court-ordered evaluations, treatment and visitation conditions imposed on the father and how non-compliance drove the case toward termination.
key_cases.quote: Due to the gravity of a proceeding to terminate parental rights, the terms of § 211.462.2 are to be strictly applied

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the termination of the mother's parental rights and remanded, holding that past acts support termination only when convincingly linked to predicted future harm, that findings supporting the earlier assumption of jurisdiction must be updated to describe the parent's condition at the time of the termination hearing, and that the trial court's findings here were insufficient on every ground relied on.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion holds that a court-ordered parenting, social services or treatment plan is relevant evidence a trial court may not ignore when it weighs termination.
key_cases.quote: To that end, a trial court cannot support a termination by merely incorporating earlier findings supporting its assumption of jurisdiction or some other earlier disposition.
